title: R.2b Linear arithmetic pass: the parallel-prefix final adder (adder substitution with a certified carry equivalence)
description:
Why: step one (skz.3) refutes miters whose cones are adder cells all the way to the outputs (multiplier_15/16bits__miter, both-seed timeouts, now 0.16-0.17 s). The 16_16 cells end in a parallel-prefix final adder: the half adders give propagate and generate, an AND/OR prefix network computes the carries, and the last XORs are the sum bits. The pass declines there (on the AND-vs-AND ultra cell side B reads 14 signals side A does not). The two AND-vs-AND 16_16 cells take 608-1707 s today, and every Booth cell (step two, skz.4) has the same final adder.

What: recognize the final adder (sum bit i = p_i xor c_i over half-adder outputs p_i, g_i) and treat each bit as a virtual full adder (a_i + b_i + c_i = s_i + 2 c_(i+1)) whose carry c_(i+1) is the prefix network's carry signal; that needs c_(i+1) <-> g_i or (p_i and c_i), a fact about the prefix network, not a cut. Prove it per bit either structurally (group generate/propagate signals G[i:j], P[i:j] recovered bottom-up, the prefix operator's associativity giving each step a short case split) or by a small CDCL call whose learned clauses are written as rup lines inside a pbc block (the sub-formula is the cone of the two carries, a few hundred gates). Then the integer check and the proof run as in step one with the virtual cells added. AMulet 2 does this substitution with a SAT call; here the certificate stays VeriPB.
acceptance_criteria: The two AND-vs-AND 16_16 cells refuted in seconds with gate-checked proofs; the fuzz (tools/arith_fuzz.py) extended with Kogge-Stone, Brent-Kung and carry-lookahead final adders and clean on 1,500 miters; no change where the pass declined before; 400-cell run off and on; Codex review clean.
notes:
2026-10-19, the real shape (16_16_and_wallace_origin_and_default_mapped_ultra_bit27, side A from output 1435 down): only output bit 27 is computed. 1435 = XNOR(167, 1434): 167 is an XOR tree over column 27's leftover bits (XOR3 shapes whose carries were removed as dead logic), 1434 is the carry into bit 27 from a prefix network of AND/NOR gates (inverted polarities, e.g. 304 = NOR(g_hi, AND(g_lo, p_hi))) over half-adder (g, p) pairs of the lower columns. The network computes only the carry into bit 27 (group signals along one tree), not each column's carry, and no lower sum bit exists in the file. So the virtual full adders need extension variables: fresh ripple carries r_(i+1) := maj(a_i, b_i, r_i) and sums s_i := a_i xor b_i xor r_i introduced by red steps (witness the fresh variable to 0 or 1, as red_const does), a lemma network carry 1434 <-> r_27 proven by a small CDCL over the cone plus the definitions with its learned clauses written as rup lines in a pbc block and checked in-process by a unit-propagation RUP checker before use (soundness without a proof file), and the same for the top column: its XOR tree equals the sum of a fresh reduction of the column bits and r_27. Several days of proof work; the payoff on 2025 is the PAR-2 of the two AND-vs-AND cells (608-1707 s today), and it is a prerequisite for every Booth cell (skz.4: three both-seed-unsolved; the two 2026 16_16 cells by name).
2026-10-21: built. Not the plan's 'adder substitution with a certified carry equivalence' over the prefix operator; the shape of the two AND-vs-AND cells asked for something more general and the design is: (1) lone sums and lone carries become cells with a fresh partner (a proof-only variable, red with a constant witness); (2) product cells for a mapper's regrouped carries (a_i b_j . a_k b_l written as a_i b_l . a_k b_j) with the proof's case split over the four inputs; (3) the carry network read as a black box: its output is the one leaf no cell of the side produces; a virtual ripple chain of fresh cells adds up the side's leftovers below the carry's column plus the two's complement of the side's carry-in-one constants (fixed-one variables), and kitten proves carry = chain bit over the side's whole cone (gate by gate over inputs, circuit order so kitten decides the top first), either polarity (a nor chain hands the carry over complemented; the top cell is a lone sum and reads it so); the core's learned clauses are the proof's rup lines; the lemma's two clauses cancel the carry in the weighted sums; the top block absorbs the 2^(K+1) multiples. Also: the first-reader polarity rule dropped (negated leaf readings are fine in the forms), real cells resolved first and unshared sides flipped whole to agree on the products, find_adders pairing by shared readers and nearest variable (not a sum's private and-nots), one cell per leaf set per side, dead-end cells dropped only when no gate reads them, grid weights for products no cell reads. Results: 16_16_and_wallace_origin_and_default_mapped_ultra_bit27 and 16_16_default_mapped_ultra_and_and_dadda_mapped_bit28 UNSAT in 0.12 s each with gate-checked proofs (35,607 and 28,625 lines; S.8: 1582 s and 793 s); the two step-one miters unchanged; sweep over the 400 cells (log/structarith-fire-2026-10-21b): fires on exactly those 4, no panic, declining cost median 19.8M (cap 20M, as before). Tests: 8 in tests/structarith.rs (prefix adders Kogge-Stone/Brent-Kung/Sklansky/ripple, pruned or not, inverted polarities, tampered chain lemma rejected, faulty prefix network left SAT); fuzz tools/arith_fuzz.py with the new shapes: 3,000 miters on two seeds all agree, 1,156 fired with checked proofs (log/arith-fuzz-2026-10-21*.txt). Gates: smoke 9/9, cargo test all 11 targets. README: 'The final-adder step'. Booth cells still decline (skz.4).
Review (Codex, gpt-6-astra max): 6 rounds. R1: proof-only variable numbers shared with the parity engine (Derived::last_var; was a clash when the engine took the proof over), lemma clause order deterministic (hash order moved kitten's decisions and the work clock), kitten lemma solving in 1M-tick pieces polling the live stop flag. R2: a carry read twice by the compared sum gave a false UNSAT (now exactly one read), product grid order. R3: traversal of the cells over the carry quadratic and unbudgeted (now by-leaf index + stopped()), constant sum overflow (now modulo 2^(K+1) as it goes). R4: a fixed one alone at the chain's top column became the chain's bit with nothing to cancel: false UNSAT (now declined; fixed ones weighted in the union-find; fixture tests/fixtures/fixed_one_chain_bit.cnf). Own re-derivation: the chain's bit removed from its own weight only; the complemented lemma proven over the flipped definitions before they are written. R5/R6 clean (900 and 1,200 generated cases on Codex's side). Fuzz: 4,500 miters on three seeds (31, 57 + the earlier) all ok. Final sweep on the frozen binary (log/structarith-fire-2026-10-21c): the same 4 cells fire, 0 panics, declining cost unchanged. Snapshot solver/13-j2-final-adder-snapshot (sha256 e57e0a8e507378b7). Paired run launched 2026-10-21 15:19: log/abtest-struct-final-adder-400-2026-10-21-15-19-20 (base --structarith=0 v final, 1800 s, one seed).
close_reason: Built, reviewed (6 Codex rounds, clean), measured. The two AND-vs-AND 16x16 cells refuted in 0.1 s with gate-checked proofs (were 1663 s and 865 s with the pass off under 1800 s; 1582 s and 793 s in S.8); the two miters as before; nothing else fires on the 400 cells; the search unchanged elsewhere (310 of 312 both-solved cells with the same conflict count, the other two being these). Paired run log/abtest-struct-final-adder-400-2026-10-21-15-19-20: 313 v 311 solved, PAR-2 400,978 v 411,558, tick PAR-2 0.965x, no contradiction (the two status swaps are wall luck on an unchanged search: oski killed at 96% of the needed work, booth_dadda at 82%). title: R.2 Linear arithmetic pass, step one: miters whose two cones share their partial products, option structarith
description:
Why: after the partial products a multiplier is linear. Two adder trees (Wallace, Dadda, origin, mapped) summing the same weighted bits give the same integer, and that is a counting fact resolution cannot prove compactly: the 16_16 cells take 10-28 minutes or time out at 16 bits. Cutting planes proves it in a page, and the structure pass already writes VeriPB.

What: a pass in the structure stage behind option structarith (default off until measured) with its own work limit. Recover adders from the buffered formula (the census code ported), infer weights, identify the two cones and their shared leaves (kissat's congruence closure already equates the AND products; the pass checks sharing on the input clauses), derive each cone's integer value as a telescoping sum, derive equality of the outputs bit by bit, and refute the miter; when the formula is not a plain miter, hand the output-equality binaries to the solver as derived clauses instead. Proof as in R.1. Report what the pass found and how much it cost on its exit line.

Targets: the 16_16 cells with the same partial-product scheme on both sides (and_wallace vs and_dadda, booth_dadda vs booth_wallace, origin vs mapped). Booth-vs-AND miters are step two (R.3).
acceptance_criteria: The same-scheme 16_16 miters refuted in seconds with proofs the gate checks; tests in tests/structure.rs (a toy miter through the gate, a tampered proof rejected, off means off, the pass's work in the work clock); stock trajectory unchanged with the option off (tools/parity.py); 400-cell run off and on at two seeds, every answer through the gate, reported per family; Codex review loop clean.

title: R.1 Toy VeriPB check of the linear pass's certificate: adder equalities, telescoping sum, bit equality
description:
Why: the linear pass stands or falls on its proof. Every step is a standard cutting-planes operation on paper; the project rule is that such a claim gets a worked toy case before it goes anywhere.

What: a small generator (scratch, then tools/ if kept) that builds two different adder trees over the same inputs (for example three 3-bit words summed in two orders, ripple-carry), the miter clause that says one output bit differs, and the VeriPB proof: per full adder the two inequalities of a plus b plus c equals s plus 2 carry, derived inside a proof-by-contradiction block by about ten rup steps (the case split on carry, then sum, then the inputs; half adders alike); the telescoping sum as one pol line with the column weights as multipliers; the two cones' sums subtracted so the shared inputs cancel; then per output bit from the top: weaken the lower literals and divide by the bit's weight to get the two equality clauses; finally the miter clause against them. Also a tampered proof (one adder equation changed) that VeriPB must reject.
acceptance_criteria: VeriPB 3 accepts the proof of the toy miter; the tampered proof is rejected; the script and both logs are under log/; the derivation template is written down in the bead notes for the Rust port.
notes: 2026-10-19 done: tools/arith_toy_proof.py writes the miter, the OPB and the VeriPB 3 proof; accepted for 4-bit (xor3 and and2 styles), 8-bit and 16x16 (2593 vars, 8613 clauses, 480 cells, 10284 lines, 300 KB, VeriPB 0.03 s); tampered proofs rejected. Derivation template for the Rust port: per cell pbc with rup case split (FA ge: c; ~s v a; ~s v b; ~s v c_in; ~s; ~a; ~b; ~c_in; empty. FA le: ~c; s v ~a; s v ~b; s v ~c_in; s; a; b; c_in; empty. HA ge rhs 3: c; empty. HA le rhs 2: ~a; ~b; empty). ge rhs is always 3 (-s-2c in literal form), le rhs is the number of inputs. pbc consumes 1 + subproof-lines ids before its result. Telescoping: pol with 2^weight multipliers; the two sides added; per bit from the top: weaken lower variables, divide by 2^w, cancel the bit by adding 2^w times the other direction's clause; a one-sided bit is proven zero from the other direction's constraint. Final: one unit rup then the empty clause. Logs under log/arith-toy-proof-*.
close_reason: Toy certificate accepted by VeriPB up to 16x16; tampered proof rejected; template recorded in the notes and the README

title: R.0 Recovery census on the 2025 cells: gates, adder cells, weights, words, blocks, miter shape
description:
Why: every backend of the epic depends on how much of each cell's netlist comes back from the clauses, and that is unknown. The 2026-10-06 census (tools/rl_structure.py) counted gates, XORs and at-most-one groups only.

What: a tool tools/netlist_census.py that, per cell (the first 3M clauses on big cells, as before): recovers gates (Tseitin patterns for AND, XOR, ITE, equivalence; general definitions by the resolvent test, with truth tables when the support is small); finds half and full adders by truth tables over 2- and 3-input cuts (XOR2 with AND2, XOR3 with majority, either polarity); chains adders into a weight assignment (union-find with offsets: sum keeps the weight, carry doubles it) and reports whether it is consistent; groups adder-network leaves into AND grids over two sets of primary inputs (the operands of a multiplier) or marks them nonstandard (Booth); reports the miter shape (cones, compared outputs); counts internal equivalence candidates by random simulation of the recovered netlist (signature collisions). Output benchmarks/rl/netlist_2025.tsv and a report under log/, with the 14 multiplier cells ranked: reachable by the linear pass, needs the Booth step, out of reach. The 2026 suite is not analysed.

First slice: the 12 16_16 cells, multiplier_15bits__miter_23, multiplier_16bits__miter_22, then the whole suite.
acceptance_criteria: Table for all 400 cells with gate coverage, adder counts and coverage, weight consistency, operands found, PP sharing between the two cones, equivalence candidates, miter shape; the 14 multiplier cells ranked; report in log/ and a dated note in the solver README; no solver change.
notes:
2026-10-19, multiplier slice done (tools/netlist_census.py, log/netlist-census-2026-10-19/mult_slice.tsv; README 'Recovery census, the multiplier slice'). Gate coverage 97-99 percent on all 14 cells. multiplier_16bits__miter_22 and multiplier_15bits__miter_23: two multipliers over one shared grid, both cones 100 percent inside adder cells, weights consistent: the linear pass refutes them as designed. The two AND-vs-AND 16_16 cells: 90-95 percent per cone, the rest a parallel-prefix final adder (half adders as propagate/generate, AND trees as the prefix network): needs the adder-substitution step in the pass. Booth-vs-AND: AND side 82-95 percent, Booth side 22-53 percent (partial-product logic, step two; mapped Booth trees lose about half their adders to an unknown cell shape). Tool lessons: occurrence cap 64 lost the Booth encoders (now 2048); two real gates imply a third definition between them, so direction is settled forward with deadlock = primary input; XOR gates are reversible, fan-out is the only local signal under renumbering. title: Netlist recovery for solver 13: recover gates, adder cells, words and arithmetic blocks from the CNF and feed them to certified reasoning backends
description:
Why: of the 72 cells unsolved on both seeds in the run of record (log/abtest-struct-lazy-400-2026-10-17-08-31-04, every structure pass and the parity engine on), about 40 are industrial or arithmetic: 16x16 multiplier miters (3-5 unsolved, the other 7-9 solved at 608-1707 s), two more multiplier miters, div/sqrt miters, two sorter miters, three oisc program unrollings, timetables, argumentation. The C kissat fails them too. The structure pass showed the pattern that works: recognise structure in the input, reason about it in the proof system that fits (GF(2) for parity, cutting planes for counting), certify with VeriPB, hand the rest to search.

What: one recovery layer with several reasoning backends. Layer 0, gates (Tseitin patterns, general definitions; kissat has this). Layer 1, cells: half and full adders, compressors, muxes, 1-bit compares, found by truth tables over small cuts so technology mapping does not hide them. Layer 2, words: carry chains order bits and fix weights, AND grids a_i and b_j name the two operands. Layer 3, blocks: a times b, a plus b, popcount, compare, found by function extraction (walking the output polynomial back through the adders proves the block's function at the same time) or by simulation against templates. Layer 4, the datapath: miter shape, two cones with compared outputs.

Backends: linear and polynomial normalisation for arithmetic miters (after the partial products a multiplier is linear; two adder trees over the same weighted inputs telescope to the same integer; cutting planes proves it), counting over recovered popcounts and comparators (structcount, and an in-search at-most-k engine for satisfiable cells), parity (gauss) over recovered XOR trees, word-level cut-point equivalences proven by kitten and logged as RUP, CSP decoding over one-hot words. IC3 over de-unrolled BMC cells is a separate backend with its own detection (the unrolling) and a plain DRAT certificate.

Order: the recovery census first (no solver code), the certificate toy check, then the linear pass as the first backend on the multiplier miters, then the counting backend, with the IC3 probe and the sweeping idea gated by their own measurements. Each pass behind a kissat-style option, off until measured on the 400 cells at two seeds; the 2026 suite stays out of all structural analysis and is consulted once per promoted candidate (plan section 8).

Session of 2026-10-18/19 with the owner; the measured facts are in the solver README under 'Next: netlist recovery (2026-10-19)'.
acceptance_criteria: Each child measured on the 400 cells with its option off and on at two seeds, every answer through the gate; the recovery census table committed; the owner's go/no-go decisions recorded in the decision beads.

description: Why: on 2026-10-12 a probe of the 94 cells the default configuration leaves unsolved found 8 satisfiable ones that kissat's own local search solves once it is given real time (--walkeffort=100000 or --walkinitially=1 --walkeffort=1000000, 300 s limit, every model checked): Ptn-7824-b19 0.7 s, mp1-Nb7T45 12 s, lockchart-group2 L18 20 s and L19_3 28 s, ER_400_20_7 apx_1 86 s and apx_2 246 s, reconf10_70_queen14_2 162 s, oddball_57_5 287 s. title: S.1 Parity pass: XOR constraint extraction and Gaussian elimination, option structparity
description: Why: 4 unsolved cells (the Tseitin formulas) are pure XOR systems that one sum of all equations refutes, 23 cells carry half or more of their clauses in XOR constraints, and kissat already extracts XOR gates for congruence closure but never treats them as a linear system. What: in the structure pass, extract XOR constraints (groups of clauses over the same variables that forbid exactly one parity, including constraints with no output variable; the detector of tools/rl_structure.py is the reference), run Gaussian elimination over GF(2), feed back the result as units, binary equivalences or the empty clause, and log the derivation (VeriPB with extension variables after Gocht and Nordstrom 2021, or DRAT with extension variables after Philipp and Rebola-Pardo 2016; choose by checker time on the Tseitin cells). Option structparity (bool, default off until measured; the promotion flips the default and keeps the off switch). Budget: a work bound so the pass stays under 2 percent of the tick budget on cells it does not help. Follow-up bead: XOR reasoning inside search (CDCL with parity) for par32, grs and the xor-op cells. Acceptance: the five Tseitin cells answered UNSAT with a checked proof in seconds; no change in answers or trajectory on cells without XOR constraints (parity.py against the C with the option off, and tick-identical with the option on where no constraint is found); solved count on the 400 cells reported with the option off and on.
notes: Step two, 2026-10-13: the flip symmetries of any formula as the solutions of a linear system over GF(2) (clauses grouped by variable set, each group's flips, elimination, one flip per free variable, each checked against every group it touches), fixing the free variable to true. xor_op_n36/n40 (every variable replaced by the XOR of two) from timeout to under a second, xor_op_n38 1492 s to 1 s. Seven Codex rounds on the step (five with one work-limit finding each, then the accounting was rewritten under one rule; two clean) and one clean round on the final tree. Still open under this bead: sums of XOR constraints that mix with other clauses (Gaussian elimination with a proof); par32-2 is the one 2025 cell with such a system and needs XOR reasoning inside search (bead 1v2.7).

title: [G] Evaluation discipline for every RL gate
description:
The rules every comparison and gate in this project follows. Gate beads link here. Re-read before launching one.

- Three arms every time: stock (policy off), policy-on with the stock action (measures logging and inference overhead alone), and the candidate.
- Metric order: solved instances, then tick PAR-2 on the work clock W (never search_ticks), then wall PAR-2. Report per family.
- Splits: sat-comp-2025 (400) and the medium suite (100, fully inside 2025) are training data. A family-stratified validation split of about 100 cells from 2025 is held out of all fitting and used for checkpoint selection. sat-comp-2026 is the true holdout and is run at most once per promoted candidate (solver 12 lesson: 296 v 292 on 2025, 160 v 197 on 2026).
- Choose what to gate with tick-budgeted deterministic runs (SAT_LIMIT_TICKS = B_cell). Only wall runs are promotion evidence. Plus or minus 2 solved is noise on 100 cells, so the 400-cell wall run plus the deterministic comparison are the decision evidence; the medium gate stays the repo's formal promotion gate.
- Promoted candidates are also run on variable-renamed, clause-shuffled copies of the validation split. A win that disappears under shuffle is input-order luck and does not count. Locality features are the most exposed.
- Correctness is absolute: a wrong answer, an invalid model, a missing or invalid proof, or a premature UNKNOWN fails the gate with no trade. Fork siblings must agree on SAT/UNSAT.
- Resource cap: at most 32 solver processes and 16 GB per process; paired arms split the cores; marginal wall timing is invalid while another sweep runs. Check for live processes before launching.

Plan: sections 4 and 8. CLAUDE.md: 'Evaluation' and 'Correctness is absolute'.
acceptance_criteria: Stays open for the life of the project. Every gate bead links here with a related dependency, and its result records all three arms per family.

title: R.11 Divider and square-root miters: census first, then a backend
description: Why: div_miter_lec__2 times out on both seeds, div-mitern172 takes about 80 s, sqrt-mitern169 to 171 take 97 to 564 s, and the 2026 suite has DivS cells and a sqrt miter by file name (solver README, Next: netlist recovery). The arithmetic pass gets nowhere on them: div_miter_lec__2 recovers no gates; the others recover gates out of circuit order (83 to 178 that cannot be ordered), only 21 to 75 adder cells, and a side of 3 gates. A divider is not linear after one step the way a multiplier is: a = q d + r with r below d, and the computer-algebra methods for dividers need that remainder bound as an extra fact. What: a census of these cells with no solver code (which circuits, restoring or non-restoring arrays, which signals the miter compares, why the gate order deadlocks); then a decision on the backend (the multiplier pass over the identity a = q d + r with the bound proven apart, or cut-point equivalences row by row).
acceptance_criteria: Census in the solver README with the backend decision recorded; for a chosen backend, a toy divider miter refuted with a gate-checked proof before any benchmark cell.
notes:
2026-10-25: div_miter_lec__2 recovers no gates only for lack of budget: with structarithticks=200000 the pass reads 45,596 gates (3,735 out of order), 795 cells, then picks a 3-gate side and stops (no multiplier). hhyp_cec_multi_2 (skz.16): gate recovery does not finish even at 200M (885K clauses).

2026-10-27, census (tools/divsqrt_census.py, benchmarks/rl/divsqrt_2025.tsv, log/divsqrt-census-2026-10-27): every clause belongs to the gate its first literal names (ABC write_cnf shape: gates of at most 4 inputs, the miter root var 2 = xor of one signal per side, a constant last); read that way every group is a definition. Gates whose clauses also define an input: 254-5,700 per cell, and the numbering is in neither order, which is why the arithmetic pass deadlocks. All five are one-output cones of the EPFL arithmetic circuits (matching the SAT Competition 2022 'Equivalence Checking of EPFL Benchmarks' description: EPFL golden v best-LUT-6 implementation): div-mitern172 quotient bit 49 and div_miter_lec__2 quotient bit 5 of the 64/64 divider (inputs a[k..63], b[0..63], the output negated), sqrt-mitern169/170/171 root bits 46/47/48 of the 128-bit square root. Both sides follow the restoring recurrence: every quotient or root bit and most remainder bits have a twin signal in each side. Cut-point chain (each twin pair proven by the stock solver on the circuit without the miter's unit, rows top down): div-mitern172 67 of 93 pairs (the top six rows are the optimised side's don't-cares), 91K conflicts in all, then the miter in 0 conflicts (search 0.8-0.9M); sqrt 90/90, 107/107, 131/131 pairs, 136-194K conflicts, then 0 (search 1.6M-7.4M). ABC iprove (measurement only) 6.7-49 s on the four. div_miter_lec__2: chain and ABC running.

2026-10-27, later: the chain on div_miter_lec__2 (unsolved at 3,600 s by solver 13 and the C kissat): 1,591 of 1,600 pairs proven (9 false matches dropped), 2.9M conflicts over 1,812 checks (3,537 s of solver time; the compared bit q5 alone 579K), then the miter in 0 conflicts. Better sampling (divisors of random bit length) removed the false matches of the first version. Certificate (tools/divsqrt_proof.py, sub-calls --plain): toys n=6-12 and the four small cells pass tools/proof_gate.py (8-16 MB, 11-27 s), three broken proofs rejected on each; sub-call work 0.18-0.41G against search's 2.1-22.4G (run S.8). div_miter_lec__2's stitched proof: 1.01 GB, drat-trim running. Codex review: rounds 1-3 changed the tools (crash v budget-stop classification, a 16 GB cap per sub-call, missing counters kept apart, tamper controls must reject), round 4 clean. Commits b6c0a2c, f82c372, 83290ac, 320734e.

2026-10-27, done but the decision: div_miter_lec__2's stitched DRAT proof (sub-calls --plain) is 13.6M lines (1.01 GB) and passes tools/proof_gate.py in 2,317 s (drat-trim); 1,812 pair checks, 5.9M conflicts, 30.6G on the work clock, against search's 40-45G at 1,800 s and 85.6G at 3,600 s, both without an answer. Write-up: solver README, 'Divider and square-root miters: census and certificate'. Open: the owner's decision, (a) build the chain as a structure pass (recommended, with the sub-call proof engine reusable for skz.10), (b) general sweeping first (skz.10), (c) park.

Decided 2026-10-27 (owner: 'Let's do A'): build the chain as a structure pass in solver 13, with the sub-call proof engine reusable for skz.10; new bead SAT-playground-skz.23.
close_reason: Met its acceptance. Census in the solver README (Divider and square-root miters: census and certificate; tools/divsqrt_census.py, benchmarks/rl/divsqrt_2025.tsv): the five cells are one-output EPFL div and sqrt miters whose sides both follow the restoring rows; the row-by-row chain decides all five (div_miter_lec__2, unsolved at 3,600 s, with 1,591 of 1,600 pairs). Certificate checked on toy dividers first, then every cell (tools/divsqrt_proof.py, one DRAT proof through tools/proof_gate.py, three broken proofs rejected). Decision recorded: the owner chose option (a), the chain as a structure pass, bead skz.23. Codex review: rounds 1-3 changed the tools, round 4 and the README review clean.

title: R.3e Multiplier miters the arithmetic pass does not read: lec_mult_CvW_11x10 and hhyp_cec_multi_2
description: Why: two multiplier equivalence checks of 2025 never reach the arithmetic lemmas (log/structarith-fire-2026-10-24-300M-final5): lec_mult_CvW_11x10 (search solves it in about 313 s) gets 212 cells, then no two separate cones among its 21 compared signals, so the cone-overlap rule rejects every pair (two 11 by 10 multipliers that likely share their partial products and more); hhyp_cec_multi_2 (a timeout on both seeds) gets no gates at all, so look at its encoding first. What: measure each reason (the overlap of the compared cones, the clause shapes gate recovery misses), then fix what fits the multiplier pass.
acceptance_criteria: Each cell refuted with a gate-checked proof, or its reason measured and written in the solver README; the cells that fire today still fire; review clean.
notes: 2026-10-27, lead from skz.17: hhyp_cec_multi_2 reads exactly by first literal (tools/divsqrt_census.py's Netlist: 194,410 gates, 256 inputs, one root var 2 = xor(3, 92166), one constant), the same ABC write_cnf shape as the EPFL div and sqrt miters, so its gate reading needs no direction search. My guess, not checked: one output bit of the EPFL hypotenuse circuit (two 128-bit operands, sqrt(a^2 + b^2)), so squarers plus a square-root recurrence; the census's chain might apply to its square-root part.

title: R.3d The three Booth cells left after skz.14: Booth against Booth, the mapped AND side's top, the Dadda top
description:
Why: skz.14 refuted bit29 (seven of the ten Booth cells of 2025 refute); three remain, their reasons measured on skz.14's final build (solver README, "Booth, step four", "What is left"):
- booth_dadda_mapped_and_booth_wallace_mapped (a timeout): the pair is now bit 30 of both sides, both read by function; the pass stops with neither side settled, as no side reads a product grid. A grid from the Booth operands (the stage hands out the data and the digits' bits) would settle both. The miter compares all 32 bits, so a refutation then needs every pair proven: a loop over the pairs, or the lower bits read from the top lemma's rungs.
- booth_dadda_mapped_and_and_wallace_mapped_bit28 (search near 1600 s): the pair and the weights are right now; the AND side, a mapped Wallace AND tree, leaves 2060, 1589 and 3097 unexplained, products folded into the final adder's logic; the product rows read 201 cells against 224 structural (21 matches fail the exact check on cuts of ten signals).
- booth_dadda_mapped_and_and_wallace_origin_bit28 (search near 1500 s): the ladder proves all 25 rungs for 8M, the last step does not close within 1000M. At column 25 the network's half adder (148, 167) loses to a full adder over (171, 148, 167) whose sum the network never computes (the third-leaf rule); a stricter rule was tried and dropped.
Also: the stage should read the generator's +1 half adder over a row bit and its sign (its sum the product the row bit reads) the other way round, as the structural pass does; then the mapped AND toy of tests/structarith.rs refutes too.
Also (owner's request, 2026-10-24): the by-function reading without a Booth side. Today the stage starts only from Booth rows, and the product rows of an AND side only from a Booth side's operands, so a miter of two mapped AND multipliers gets the structural reading alone. Give the stage the operand order another way: from the product grid of a side the structural cells read (the main pass already places every input along its operand from weighted product gates), or, when both sides fold their products, from the inputs and the simulation (product_bit_of already checks an operand order against the compared bit; the order itself needs finding, for example from the lowest output bits, bit 0 being a0 b0). The same operands give the Booth-against-Booth cell its grid. Acceptance for this part: toy miters of two mapped AND multipliers (one side in the generator's form, then both folded) refute with gate-checked proofs; the 2025 AND-against-AND cells that fire keep firing.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three cells refuted with a gate-checked proof, or its reason measured again on the final build; two mapped AND multipliers against each other read by function (toys refuted with gate-checked proofs); the cells that fire today still fire with checked proofs; fuzz, the 300M sweep against the previous build and the toy grids clean; review clean.
notes:
2026-10-24, first session (solver README, "Booth, step five"):
- Booth against Booth (booth_dadda_mapped_and_booth_wallace_mapped): the pass now proves the top pair, bit 31, equal (2 derived clauses, 4.4 s, 144M work; the VeriPB stage accepts them, run alone with its negative control). The cell stays unsolved: the miter compares all 32 product bits.
- Changes: a grid from the Booth operands when no side reads plain products (both sides then settle); the stage's top column by function (the product bit the compared signal is); two producers of one signal tied in the polarity reading (both Booth stages found the same two sign-bit cells; the untied copy's readers read its outputs the other way round, which kitten's counterexample a=0x8ace b=0xec0f exposed).
- Whole word, measured: forced pairs (SAT_STRUCT_DEBUG_FORCE_PAIR): bits 7, 12, 16 stop early (12 to 14 signals at a middle bit's top: that column's cells are half outside its cone), bits 24, 28, 30 run out of the lemma allowance. Cells found on the whole multiplier fix the tops but flip the low columns' reading (cells far above the bit outvote them) and the lemmas still run out; keeping only in-cone cells stops earlier; sides over the whole word leave 37 final-adder signals no cell produces. Next: one of these made reliable.
- Checks: 152 tests; fuzz seed 35000 ok; 300M sweep against skz.13's build (log/structarith-fire-2026-10-24-300M-skz15a): 12 fire against 10, none lost; toy grids none lost; the seven refuted cells gate ok; smoke 9/9.
- Not started yet: the AND-against-AND reading (operand order from the structural cells' product weights, then the toys), the mapped AND side's top, the Dadda top.
2026-10-24, the AND-against-AND reading, first try (no code kept): toy miters of a column-wise AND multiplier against the mapped AND toy, and of two mapped AND toys (opposite compressor orders), 8 and 12 bits, pruned to bits 9, 12, 18. Today all six stop with signals no cell produces. Operands from the product gates a side's structural cells read (weights by a union-find over the cells, inputs placed with operand_positions) came out 7 by 7 on the 8-bit toys: the origin side's cells read no product of a0 or of b7, so the compared bit is no product bit of those operands and the product rows do not start; the origin side also fails on its own in these pruned toys (6 signals no cell produces); with both sides folded there are too few product gates. Needed: operand discovery that does not rest on product gates (the 4-input folded cells pair a_i with b_j; the positions from the simulation), and a look at why the pruned column-wise side fails alone.
2026-10-25: the Dadda top (booth_dadda_mapped_and_and_wallace_origin_bit28) is refuted since skz.19 (the full solver on the lemma's last step, 11.4 s, gate ok), so that part is done. Booth against Booth rechecked with the fallback: the forced pairs for bits 24, 28, 30 prove 11 to 17 rungs, then the last step beats the full solver too (400M work, not proven). Left: Booth against Booth (whole word), the mapped AND side's top (dadda_mapped_and_and_wallace_mapped), the AND-against-AND reading.

title: R.3c The four Booth cells left after skz.13: the mapped Dadda top, mapped AND sides, Booth against Booth
description:
Why: after skz.13 the cells by function (src/structarith/booth.rs) refute the two mapped Booth Wallace cells; four Booth cells of 2025 remain. Their reasons, measured on the final build of skz.13 (solver README, section "Booth, step three"):
- booth_dadda_mapped_and_and_wallace_origin_bit28 (search solves it near 1500 s): the stage finds 113 cells, but the Dadda tree's columns 22 to 27 keep three to six signals each: the mapper merged the last levels into the final adder (a half adder layer of xor propagates and and/nor generates and kills, a third tree signal folded in, some carries existing only inside that logic). The ladder proves 22 of 24 rungs, then kitten runs out of the 200M allowance on the last step (about 7 s before search).
- booth_dadda_mapped_and_and_wallace_mapped_bit28 (search near 1600 s, killed at the limit in one run): stops before the lemmas on its AND side, a mapped Wallace AND tree: a product cell contradicts the weights and the compared signals end one weight apart.
- booth_dadda_mapped_and_booth_wallace_mapped (a timeout in every run): a whole-word Booth against Booth compare. The pass takes one middle compared pair, the tops keep 14 and 11 signals (the virtual top takes at most six), and the compared signals end one weight apart.
- booth_wallace_origin_and_default_mapped_bit29 (search near 600 s): its AND side reads two gates no rule explains. Gate 2683 is MAJ(a1b2, a0b3, a0a1b1b2): a column-3 carry whose third leaf is the column-2 carry written over other products (gate 2680 = a0 b1 a1b2); 2788 is the network's.

What would likely work: half adders with a fresh partner in the stage (the Dadda top's xor propagates whose carries live in the final adder; the AND side's bottom carries whose sums are dead); the stage's matching with products as leaves for an AND side (operand order from the Booth side), used where the structural cells leave a side with signals no cell produces; for Booth against Booth, a compare of the top bit (or every bit) of a whole-word miter whose two sides share their row logic, and the sides' shared row bits read as common leaves.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the four cells refuted with a gate-checked proof, or its reason measured again on the final build; the cells that fire today still fire with checked proofs; fuzz and the 400-cell sweep clean; review clean.
notes:
2026-10-24, closing state (solver README, "Booth, step four"; Codex rounds 23-26, round 26 clean):

- Final build 04e999a62ce22b0a. Checks: 152 tests (two new: mapped AND toy, one-sided compare); fuzz 9,000 miters (seeds 23000 to 33000) all ok; 400-cell sweep at 300M work against skz.13's build (log/structarith-fire-2026-10-24-300M-old, -final5): 10 fire before, 11 after, none lost, no panic, no answer changed; two toy grids (200 miters) none lost; the seven refuted cells gate ok; smoke 9/9.

- Left (reasons on the final build, README): dadda_mapped_and_and_wallace_origin (25 of 25 rungs for 8M, the last step does not close within 1000M); dadda_mapped_and_and_wallace_mapped (the AND side's three gates folded into the final adder; product rows 201 against 224); booth_dadda_mapped_and_booth_wallace_mapped (no product grid on either side, neither settles; then the whole-word miter). title: R.3b Mapped Booth trees: recover the adders of a technology-mapped Booth multiplier
description:
Why: four of the ten Booth cells of 2025 have the Booth side in mapped form, and the Booth-against-Booth cell has two mapped sides. The arithmetic pass finds 60 to 80 of the about 250 adder cells there, so it declines. Step R.3 (bead skz.4) refutes the cells whose Booth side is in origin form.

What we know (2026-10-23, solver README section Booth, session three): the mapper folds the row bit's xor with the digit's sign into the first adder level. In the bottom columns only the carries survive (the sums are low product bits, dead logic in a cone pruned to one bit), and a carry is built as a mux: in 16_16_booth_wallace_mapped_and_and_wallace_origin_bit28, gate 1374 is not (p ? q : b3), which is the complement of MAJ(q, p xor b3, b3), the row bit and the +neg. A sum is built from its carry and leaves, so its cone holds the carry. Many unexplained signals depend on 7 to 12 inputs: sums of two or three row bits built as one structure. Tried in a scratch build: lifting two-signal sums into three-signal fused cells, and fused lone carries with fresh sums. Each gave 0 to 2 cells, not enough.

What would likely work: recover adders by function. For each unexplained gate, take its function over the inputs (support up to about 12), and match it against XOR and MAJ of candidate row-bit functions (known from the selector groups and the operand grid) and of signals already recovered. The cells then have virtual row-bit leaves (fresh variables defined by truth tables over 5 inputs) and case splits over their support. Also in scope: the AND default-mapped side of 16_16_booth_wallace_origin_and_default_mapped_bit29 reads two gates no rule explains (2683, which is a1b2 and (a0 and g2679 or a0b3), and 2788): a mapped product-cell shape.
acceptance_criteria: The four mapped-Booth-against-AND cells, the Booth-against-Booth cell and wallace_origin_and_default_mapped_bit29 refuted with gate-checked proofs, or the reason measured per cell; fuzz and the 400-cell sweep clean; review clean.
notes: 2026-10-24 (continued): Codex review rounds 21-22. Round 21 (three P2): stale cell indexes when both sides are read by function (both removals now before either side's cells are placed; test two_mapped_booth_sides_are_both_read_by_function), a negated row bit's weighted copy losing its sign (copy of the variable, literal keeps the sign), the row-gate scan skipping its only limit check (polls before early continues, tables reserved first; 4.41M under a 4.27M limit -> about 14K over). Round 22 clean. Gates: smoke 9/9, cargo test all pass, the fourteen 2025 cells with proofs through the gate (ten fire, all ok), fuzz 3000 clean, sweep log/structarith-fire-2026-10-24b clean. Open: the four cells listed in the README section 'Booth, step three' (dadda top merged into the final adder; dadda AND side weights; Booth v Booth whole word; bit29 AND side).
close_reason: Met its acceptance (owner's decision 2026-10-24): booth_wallace_mapped_and_and_wallace_origin_bit28 and booth_wallace_mapped_and_default_origin_bit28 refuted with gate-checked proofs in 0.6 s (commit 9e59fbb, the cells by function, src/structarith/booth.rs); the other four cells' reasons measured on the final build (solver README 'Booth, step three'); fuzz 3000 clean, 400-cell sweep clean, review rounds 21-22 clean. The four cells continue in the follow-up bead.

title: S.10 Parity engine follow-ups: no matrix on equivalence-only cells; cut the proof-checking cost
description:
Why: the README's 'left for a later candidate' after the gauss promotion (2026-10-18). (a) On 46 of the 107 cells where the engine builds a matrix the rows are equivalences only; kissat's substitution handles those, the engine can reason nothing, and the two timetable losses of the paired run were exactly that coin flip. (b) bivium's proof stream was 3.6 GB and 71 minutes to check; the engine's proofs cost two checker timeouts more than stock; on the small case only 64 of 913 engine clauses were in drat-trim's core.

What: (a) skip the build when every extracted XOR has two variables (or when the matrix after helper reduction has no row of three or more), measured on the 107 cells and the 400. (b) derive a clause's proof only when it is needed: engine clauses exempt from vivification, strengthening and collection until their derivation is written, or written at the first rewrite; measured on bivium and par32-2 by proof size and VeriPB time.
acceptance_criteria: (a) no change on the other 61 matrix cells' trajectories except where the skip applies; 400-cell run at two seeds. (b) proof size and check time on bivium and par32-2 before and after; every answer through the gate; review clean.
notes: 2026-10-20, found in S.8 (1v2.10): the engine's on/off decision depends on the proof file. fits() in src/gauss.rs counts the proof's table of row sets (rows x rows bits) in gausslimit only when a proof is written, so a run with a proof can leave the engine off where a run without one turns it on. dislog_a14_x14_n24: without a proof the matrix (6,904 rows x 21,545 columns) is built, yields 41 propagations and the engine switches itself off (solved at 517 s); with a proof '10920 XORs over 21545 variables exceed gausslimit=256M bits' and it never starts (11,299,122 conflicts, 1782 s). sum_of_3_cubes_37_bits_87 differs slightly too (W 90.63G v 90.49G). 339 of the 344 S.8-solved cells do identical work either way. Runs without proofs (run_kissat_full.sh) and with them (feature_ablation, the competition) can therefore take different searches on parity cells. Option to decide: count the table always, so every run behaves as the competition run does (the engine is then off on such cells in no-proof runs too); measure on the parity cells before changing it.

title: R.7 Decision: port an IC3 engine with an unrolling detector, or close the line
description: Decide from the R.6 probe. Yes if the invariants come in seconds on cells we take hundreds of seconds or time out on: then R.8 builds the detector and the engine. No if IC3 is as slow as search on them. Also to weigh: the 2026 suite has few BMC-shaped cells by name (oski15a01b15s, an xits miter, a CBMC unrolling), so the transfer is weaker than for the arithmetic families. Owner's call.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict recorded with the probe numbers.

title: R.6 Run: IC3 probe on de-unrolled BMC cells (measurement only, external model checker)
description:
Why: a bounded-model-checking CNF is k copies of a transition relation with the initial state on copy 0 and the bad state on copy k. CDCL must refute every k-step path in one formula of size k times a frame; IC3 works on one frame and finds an invariant that holds at every depth, which proves the unrolling UNSAT. Its reasoning is clausal, so the certificate is plain DRAT (the invariant re-derived frame by frame with renamed variables). Whether it is fast on our cells is the unknown: these designs are in the SAT competition because their BMC was slow at HWMCC too.

What: a scratch script that de-unrolls three or four 2025 cells whose period the census knows (valves-gates-1-k617 at 985K variables, about 1.6K per frame, 1533-1689 s UNSAT; SAT_dat.k100, period 15562, 778-963 s; x-epic_a19-p16_step, period 30862, 433-511 s; g2-hwmcc15deep-oski15a10b10s-k20, timeout) into AIGER (frame 0 extras as the initial state, the repeating frame as the transition relation, the last frame's extras as the bad state, variables that cross a frame boundary as latches), and runs an existing IC3 (rIC3, the HWMCC 2024/2025 winner, or ABC's pdr) on them as a measurement tool only, the way Satsuma served the symmetry census; the repo rule of no external solver in the shipped binary stands. Record the invariant sizes and times against our times.
acceptance_criteria: A table of the probed cells with de-unrolling success, IC3 result, time and invariant size against solver 13's time; the script and logs under log/; a dated note in the solver README; the decision bead R.7 gets the numbers.
notes:
2026-10-19: checkers for the probe. rIC3 1.5.2 from crates.io needs a nightly toolchain (installed: rustup nightly, minimal) and then fails on bitwuzla (needs meson) and kissat bindings (need clang), neither on the host; not pursued. ABC with pdr (IC3) built from github berkeley-abc/abc at depth 1 with 'make -j ABC_USE_NO_READLINE=1' (readline headers are missing); the binary is at tools/checkers/abc/abc (git-ignored, like VeriPB). The de-unrolling script is still to write: gate recovery per frame from tools/netlist_census.py, the frame shift from the census period, latches as the variables whose definition crosses the frame boundary, AIGER out.
2026-10-19, first look at SAT_dat.k100 (scratch analysis, pinned to the free cores): the clauses do repeat at a variable offset of 15,562 (93 % of sampled clauses reappear shifted by it; 105 frames), units sit in frames 99-103 (about 9,400 each). But it is not a clean safety unrolling: 4.5M clauses stay inside one frame and 1.59M reach the next, yet 168K reach two frames over and about 2,000 reach 97-98 frames over (the property relates early states to late ones); frames 98-104 have a different, small structure (10 shared variables per step); and adjacent standard frames share about 5,800 variables through their crossing clauses, far more than a latch interface, so the true frame boundary is likely not at a multiple of the offset. A faithful AIGER model would need: the boundary search (the shift that minimizes crossing clauses), the latch set (variables both read across the boundary and defined by the previous frame), extra frozen latches carrying the initial state forward for the long-range clauses, and gate recovery per frame to turn the transition clauses into AND gates. That is a research spike of its own, not a one-day probe; the payoff on 2025 is PAR-2 on solved cells plus g2-hwmcc15deep and the memory-bound pj2002. Parked pending the owner's call (reported 2026-10-19).

title: R.5 Counting backend over recovered blocks: structcount step two, then an in-search at-most-k engine for satisfiable cells
description:
Why: the counting pass (bead SAT-playground-1v2.4) refutes pairwise pigeonhole shapes only. Recovered popcounts, sequential counters, totalizers and decision-diagram counts are cardinality constraints too; the oddball cells are satisfiable, so there counting has to help the search, not refute the formula.

What, in steps. (a) structcount step two: take the constraints R.4 and R.0 recover as at-most-k and at-least-k rows (built from the input clauses in VeriPB as the pass builds its group constraints today), and extend the Hall argument to k above 1 (a flow or a weighted matching instead of a matching). (b) The rook decision-diagram count stays as noted in 1v2.4 (the certificate is the cost). (c) An in-search at-most-k engine for satisfiable cells: MiniCard-style propagation (k plus 1 watches, the k true literals as the reason), reasons built lazily and tagged as the parity engine's are (Assigned::GAUSS has the pattern), each reason clause proved into the VeriPB stream from the constraint's rows by one pol line, a yield guard like gaussyield, option structcard or similar, off until measured. Native propagation adds reasoning power only where the input encoding propagates weakly (adder-based popcounts, decision diagrams); for pairwise and sequential-counter encodings it saves work only. The in-search engine moves the trajectory on every cell it touches, so two seeds.
acceptance_criteria: Step (a): the recovered-constraint pigeonhole shapes refuted with gate-checked proofs, 400-cell run off and on. Step (c): the oddball timeouts measured over two seeds against stock, every model checked; no unsatisfiable cell lost on either seed; tests as for the parity engine (off means off, the engine stopped mid-search with tagged reasons on the trail through the gate); review clean.

title: R.3 Linear arithmetic pass, step two: Booth partial products
description:
Why: half of the 12 16_16 cells compare a Booth multiplier with an AND-array one; their partial products are different signals, so the shared-leaf argument of step one does not apply.

What: each radix-4 Booth digit d_j takes one of five values (minus 2, minus 1, 0, 1, 2) given by three bits of b, with the linear identity d_j equals minus 2 b_2j+1 plus b_2j plus b_2j-1 (a small case split over the eight bit patterns). A Booth row is a times d_j; for each digit value the row's bits are a shift or complement of a, so the row's value is linear in a under that case. Introduce product extension variables (a_i and the digit indicators) with red definitions in VeriPB, derive the row value in each case with big-M conditional constraints, combine with the exactly-one over the digit values, and show both cones sum to the same degree-2 polynomial over the a_i b_k products. Sign extension and the plus-one of negative rows are template variants to recover from the netlist.
acceptance_criteria: The booth-vs-and 16_16 miters (origin and mapped) refuted with gate-checked proofs; ultra variants reported as reached or not; 400-cell run at two seeds; review clean.
notes:
2026-10-22 (session 1, partial). Design, checked on a toy first (tools/booth_toy_proof.py, VeriPB accepts, a tampered coefficient is rejected): a Booth row's weighted sum is a polynomial identity of degree 2 over products a_t b_k, proven in cutting planes by a pbc with a case split over the digit's three bits (selector set); under each case every row bit is a constant or a literal of one a bit (RUP through its gates), every product 0 or a_t (RUP), a weighted pol sum with literal axioms gives the identity plus big-M of the case's falsified literals, saturation gives the case clause, the eight resolve to the empty clause. Built in structarith.rs so far: (1) input leaves: an unproduced leaf that is a function of up to 6 inputs through gates no cell owns (products, Booth row bits, sign bits) with its truth table; fused xor leaves (fresh) lifted from their signals; (2) selector sets per leaf (up to 3 inputs under whose every assignment the leaf is a constant or one literal), grouped per side: on the origin Booth cell the groups are exactly the 9 digits ([b0,b1] 15 bits, 8 digits of 3 bits, [b15] 12 = the correction row); (3) the sides compared as polynomials over the inputs (Poly, Moebius transform) instead of as leaf sets; the constant may differ by a multiple of 2^(K+1) as before, variable coefficients must agree exactly for now (the block step would carry multiples of 2^(K+1) but that path is unexercised); (4) the netlist's circuit-order judgement ignores variables with more than one candidate definition (two muxes over one select 'define' their shared input eight times in a Booth multiplier; the odd b bits came out as gates); (5) a cell over two bare inputs feeding no cell is dropped (the digit encoder's xor+and); lone gates never take a cut with a bare input; the gates in input leaves' cones are no lone gates; (6) the fused-leaf matcher: a pair (sum, carry) over a cut whose sum+2carry polynomial is a sum of leaves one of which is x xor y (a fresh variable of the proof): the origin Booth tree folds the row bit's xnor into its adder (24 such cells per side); (7) weights: only produced signals tie cells; input leaves take the weight of the first cell reading them within a side and never tie frames (a Booth sign bit is read at two columns; a_i b_15 sits at column 15 on an AND side and 16 in a Booth correction row); the two sides are tied through the compared signals inside the lone-gate rounds, then through shared leaves; the grid rule and the product cells moved into the rounds after the tie; strict rounds defer lone cells over not-yet-written gate leaves to a relaxed round (a stale plain reading of a later lone carry's output gave a polarity conflict); (8) a side whose real cells' leaf polynomial is the negative of the other's (products read negated) is flipped whole before the virtual cells (the old 'mostly negated leaves' heuristic flipped Booth sides wrongly: xnor row bits read negated sum to the plain product); (9) the lemmas get an allowance of 10x the pass budget on top of it (the and_dadda_origin carry-skip lemma needs ~19M ticks); (10) the chain pool takes what the network reads that no cell produces: products by the grid, row bits by the template of the same selector group shifted along the operand (grid positions). title: R.15 Multiplier shapes the 2025 cells lack: signed multipliers, squarers, multiply-accumulate, constant multipliers
description: Why: the arithmetic pass and its stages were built and measured on the 2025 multiplier miters only: unsigned AND arrays and unsigned radix-4 Booth (with its correction row). Common shapes are untested: signed multipliers (Baugh-Wooley's inverted products and constant ones; signed Booth with no correction row), squarers (a times a: the operand grid's two operands are one, so placing inputs from a two-coloured pair graph fails), multiply-accumulate (one more addend row), and constant multipliers (shift and add). The 2026 holdout's shapes are not known, and this is where the pass could break unseen. What: a toy miter of each shape in tests/structarith.rs, in the generator's form and a mapped form; record what the pass reads; fix what is cheap.

title: R.14 In-search arithmetic reasoning: a propagator over the recovered adder cells, like the parity engine (decide after R.13)
description: Why: the parity engine is the one structure engine that works inside search: the XOR rows found before search propagate on partial assignments with lazy reasons. The arithmetic analogue would keep the recovered cells' column equations and propagate or explain over them during search, SMT style. The expected value is unclear: a multiplier's difficulty for CDCL sits in its non-linear carries, which column propagation does not remove, and the proof log would be VeriPB (the parity engine's VeriPB proofs cost about ten times its solve). What: only if R.13 shows that partial arithmetic facts help search, prototype the propagator on the multiplier cells and measure.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision, build or close, with the measurements behind it.

title: R.8 Unrolling detector and IC3 engine with DRAT output, option structic3
description: Why: gated by R.7. (3) DRAT output: the invariant's clauses derived on frame 0 from the initial clauses, re-derived on each next frame from the previous frame plus that frame's transition clauses by the same logged derivation renamed, and the invariant against the bad clauses on the last frame. Option structic3, off until measured.

title: S.6 XOR reasoning inside search (CDCL with parity propagation), follow-up to the parity pass
description: Why: par32-2, grs-256-64, 16_2 and the xor-op cells mix XOR constraints with clauses; a pre-pass elimination does not decide them, a parity propagator inside search (Xorcle, SAT 2026) does. What: after S.1 is measured, decide whether to add a parity propagator to the search loop with proof logging in the same format as S.1. Option structparity=2. Acceptance: a decision recorded here with the S.1 numbers; if yes, the pass measured as in S.5. Depends on S.1.
design: Design (2026-10-15). What: a parity engine inside search (option gauss, off until measured), the Han-Jiang scheme as CryptoMiniSat uses it: the XOR constraints the parity pass already extracts from the input become bit-set rows of a matrix kept in reduced row echelon form over the unassigned variables (each row has a basic variable that occurs in no other row); every row watches its basic variable and one other unassigned variable; after clause propagation reaches a fixpoint the engine reads the new trail segment, and a row whose watch was assigned either moves the watch, propagates its last unassigned variable, is satisfied, or is a conflict; when a basic variable is assigned the row takes a new basic variable and adds itself to every other row holding it (the Jordan step, which keeps the propagation complete: whatever the XOR system implies under the assignment, some row has one unassigned variable). Backtracking undoes nothing in the matrix (rows stay a basis of the same space); after inprocessing the engine re-reads every row (dirty flag). A propagation or conflict puts the row's clause (all its literals false but the propagated one) into the arena as a redundant clause: the reason, or the conflict for analyze. Rows are pure sums of input XORs (no unit substituted, no learned fact), so each reason clause is a consequence of the input alone. XOR variables are frozen: never eliminated (eliminate, fastel) nor substituted (substitute's representatives), so the matrix columns stay live. Engine work is charged to the work clock (a gauss_ticks kind in the workclock line). Proof: VeriPB stage 1 (the pass's writer stays open through search, derived.cnf is streamed and its header patched at exit): each input XOR becomes a pair of linear inequalities 'sum of its literals - 2 (carries) >= parity' and '<=' through a chain of fresh xor/and variables (red + rup + pol, about 12 lines per link and 3 * 2^k for the parity); a row addition is two pol lines (add the pairs); a reason or conflict clause of a row is ONE pol line: LE + the literal axioms of the clause's literals, divide 2, multiply 2, add GE (the odd right-hand side is what makes the division cut; verified by VeriPB on a toy with equality checks, scratchpad xor/pb/toy.py). Replaced rows are deleted from the proof. Guards: off when the input has fewer than 2 XORs or the matrix would exceed gausslimit bits; the engine may use at most gausseffort per mille of the search ticks (then it stops); with gauss=0 the solver is byte-identical. Measurement: CLAUDE.md evaluation, two seeds, plus a wall check on a quiet host for the inner-loop cost and the few-XOR cells.
notes:
2026-10-15 feasibility, before any solver code. (1) Oracle: CryptoMiniSat 5.8.0 (built in the scratchpad, Gauss-Jordan on by default) solves par32-2 in 7 s (SATISFIABLE, model checked against every clause; 110 matrix rows after it xored chain variables together, 93.6K conflicts); the stock solver never solves it (every 1800 s run). 16_2: CMS running. (2) A fixed XOR basis as chain clauses without an engine (RREF of the 2624 input XORs, 17K fresh variables, 73K clauses, scratchpad xor/basis.py) does not solve par32-2 in 900 s with the shipped binary: the in-search re-pivoting is what matters. (3) The proof recipe (design field) passes VeriPB 3.0.2 on a toy with two 3-XORs sharing a variable, with equality checks that the derived constraints are exactly the intended clauses. (4) Read: search_propagate (the hook point after the clause fixpoint), assign_reference (a reason clause whose other literals are at level 0 assigns at level 0 by itself), learn_reference (how a new clause is watched at the jump level: lits[0] the propagated literal, lits[1] the highest-level false one), the three deactivation paths eliminate / fastel / substitute, the gate (derived.cnf may raise the variable count; stage 1 proves derived clauses from the input alone).
2026-10-16, decision: built (X.1 engine, X.2 proof, X.3 guards; commits cc43d6d, 6892751, e8b0bad) and measured on both seeds; the engine solves par32-2 (12-34 s) and nothing else holds across seeds; bivium slower on both; 310 v 309, 311 v 311. Not a default. Left open for a later pass: no matrix on equivalence-only cells (46 of the 107 engine cells), the bivium slowdown, VeriPB checking at ~10x the solve time.
bivium diagnostic (seed 1, idle host, no proof): engine 842 s v stock 760 s with 2.66M v 15.96M conflicts; 16.8M engine propagations each materialized as a reason clause (row length) into the arena: search ticks per conflict 5x stock's; engine ticks 19.5G of 59.9G work; with the proof written (the paired run) 1785 s. Fix if taken up: lazy reasons (needs a proof design that survives kissat rewriting clauses).
2026-10-18: with lazy reasons (1v2.7.4) the engine is promoted: gauss default 1 (commit after 762d4c3). Left as later candidates: no matrix on equivalence-only cells; the proof checking cost.
close_reason: XOR reasoning inside search shipped: option gauss on by default since 2026-10-18 (lazy reasons), proofs the gate checks, measured on two seeds (311 v 308, 315 v 311, no UNSAT loss).

title: S.4 CSP decoding pass: one-hot blocks and binary nogoods solved as a finite-domain CSP, option structcsp
description: Why: 131 cells carry exactly-one or at-most-one groups and a specialist that decodes the CSP and runs local search solved frb80 in 2 s; the SAT side of several crafted families (frb, rbsat, sgi, crafted-n, sudoku, timetable) is a finite-domain CSP in direct encoding. What: detect exactly-one blocks covering the variables (one long positive clause plus pairwise negatives per block) with every other clause a binary negative clause between two blocks (a forbidden value pair), build the CSP, run a bounded min-conflicts local search with restarts, and on success extend the assignment by unit propagation and check it against every original clause before answering SAT; no UNSAT claims. Option structcsp (bool, default off until measured). Budget: a tick bound on the search so an unsolved CSP hands over to CDCL unchanged. Acceptance: frb80 answered SAT with a model the gate checks; the stock trajectory unchanged when the search fails; solved count on the 400 cells reported with the option off and on. Lowest priority of the four; the measured yield in our set is one cell.
notes: Design notes 2026-10-08. Detection: exactly-one blocks covering most variables (one long positive clause plus the pairwise negatives per block, from the census amo/eo detector) with every other clause a binary negative between two blocks; otherwise off. Search: min-conflicts with restarts over block values under the tick budget; a solution is extended by unit propagation and checked against every original clause before 'SAT'; no UNSAT claims, so no proof artifacts: the pass then adds the model's literals as units? No: a model is not a redundant extension unless verified; instead answer SAT directly through the application (print the model) and skip the search. That needs an application hook: run() returns an Option<model>. Cells: frb80 (verified by the random-csp specialist), maybe rbsat-v945.
